name: Broccoli
species_guidance: Safe for all 5 hamster species in moderation.
nutrition_notes: Rich in vitamins C and K, dietary fiber, and sulforaphane.
preparation: Wash thoroughly. Offer a small bite-sized floret (raw or lightly steamed without salt).

name: Cucumber
species_guidance: Safe for all species. Excellent for gentle hydration.
nutrition_notes: High water content, low calories.
preparation: Slice a 0.5cm wheel, peel if waxed. Avoid feeding excessively large pieces as high water can cause loose stools.

name: Carrot
species_guidance: Safe in small amounts for Syrians. AVOID or very rare tiny sliver for Campbell's, Winter Whites, and Chinese due to natural sugar content.
nutrition_notes: High in beta-carotene and vitamin A, but relatively high in natural sucrose.
preparation: Peel, wash, and cut into a thumbnail-sized matchstick. Never feed whole baby carrots.

name: Bell Pepper (Red, Green, Yellow)
species_guidance: Safe for all species. Green has lowest sugar, red has highest vitamin C.
nutrition_notes: Superb source of vitamin C and antioxidants.
preparation: Wash thoroughly and REMOVE ALL SEEDS and white pith. Slice into small slivers.

name: Cauliflower
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Low sugar, high fiber. Can cause mild gas if fed in large quantities.
preparation: Raw or steamed without seasoning. Feed a pea-sized piece.

name: Courgette (Zucchini)
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Mild flavor, gentle on digestion, low in natural sugars.
preparation: Wash skin thoroughly, slice into a thin quarter-circle.

name: Kale
species_guidance: Safe for all species in moderation.
nutrition_notes: High in calcium, iron, and vitamin A. Feed in moderation to prevent urinary calcium accumulation.
preparation: Rinse well, tear into small leafy portions (postage-stamp size).

name: Romaine Lettuce
species_guidance: Safe for all species. (Do NOT confuse with Iceberg Lettuce).
nutrition_notes: Nutrient dense green. NOT watery like iceberg.
preparation: Wash crisp leaf, tear a small section. Avoid wilted leaves.

name: Iceberg Lettuce
species_guidance: Unsafe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Contains lactucarium and near 96% water. Triggers rapid watery diarrhea, bloating, and dehydration in small rodents.
preparation: Do not feed. Use dark leafy greens like romaine, kale, or rocket instead.

name: Raw Potato & Potato Skin
species_guidance: Strictly toxic to all rodents.
nutrition_notes: Contains high levels of solanine and chaconine (glycoalkaloids) causing neurological and gastrointestinal toxicity.
preparation: NEVER FEED raw potato, potato sprouts, or green skin under any circumstances.

name: Onion, Garlic, Leeks, Chives & Shallots
species_guidance: Deadly toxic to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Contains thiosulfate and disulfides which induce oxidative hemolysis (destruction of red blood cells), causing fatal hemolytic anemia.
preparation: NEVER FEED raw, cooked, dried, or powdered forms. Keep all allium away from hamsters.

name: Rhubarb (Stalks & Leaves)
species_guidance: Deadly toxic to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Extremely concentrated oxalic acid crystals bind systemic calcium, causing acute renal failure and rapid death.
preparation: NEVER FEED.

name: Raw Kidney Beans & Raw Legumes
species_guidance: Deadly toxic to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Contains toxic phytohaemagglutinin (lectin) causing intestinal cell agglutination and fatal poisoning.
preparation: NEVER FEED raw beans or lentils.

name: Apple (Flesh only)
species_guidance: Occasional treat for Syrians (once weekly). Avoid for Dwarfs and Chinese due to fructose triggering diabetes.
nutrition_notes: Rich in pectin and vitamin C. SEEDS ARE DEADLY TOXIC (contain amygdalin / cyanide).
preparation: Peel optional, cut a pea-sized piece of flesh. ABSOLUTELY REMOVE ALL SEEDS AND CORE.

name: Blueberries
species_guidance: Great antioxidant treat for Syrians. Dwarfs can only have a half blueberry once a fortnight max.
nutrition_notes: Packed with anthocyanins and vitamin C.
preparation: Wash thoroughly. Syrians can have 1 berry; cut in half for dwarfs.

name: Strawberries
species_guidance: Syrians: small pea-sized treat. Dwarfs: avoid due to sugar sensitivity.
nutrition_notes: High vitamin C and natural fruit sugar.
preparation: Wash, remove green cap, cut tiny sliver.

name: Banana
species_guidance: Syrians only in micro amounts. Avoid for dwarfs.
nutrition_notes: High sugar and potassium. Very sticky texture.
preparation: Feed a paper-thin slice only by hand. Sticky banana can ferment and become impacted inside cheek pouches.

name: Citrus (Orange, Lemon, Lime, Grapefruit)
species_guidance: Harmful to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Extremely high citric acid causes severe gastric erosion, painful mouth ulcers, and urinary bladder inflammation.
preparation: NEVER FEED any citrus fruit, peel, or juice.

name: Avocado
species_guidance: Toxic to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Contains persin (fungicidal toxin) and excessive fatty oils, causing myocardial damage and respiratory distress.
preparation: NEVER FEED flesh, skin, or pit.

name: Dried Mealworms
species_guidance: Essential natural protein for all species. Roborovskis and Dwarfs relish insect forage.
nutrition_notes: High protein (approx 50%) and healthy fats.
preparation: Scatter 2-3 dried mealworms 2 to 3 times weekly. Roborovskis benefit greatly from insect foraging.

name: Black Soldier Fly Larvae (Calci Worms)
species_guidance: Superb for all species, especially growing or nursing hamsters.
nutrition_notes: Optimal calcium-to-phosphorus ratio compared to mealworms.
preparation: Feed 1-2 larvae as a healthy high-calcium forage treat.

name: Plain Boiled Chicken (Unseasoned)
species_guidance: Excellent lean protein source for all species.
nutrition_notes: Pure lean animal protein.
preparation: Boiled in plain water ONLY. No salt, pepper, oil, onions, or garlic. Shred a tiny fingernail-sized piece.

name: Plain Hard-Boiled Egg
species_guidance: Safe for all species. Particularly beneficial for elderly or convalescing hamsters.
nutrition_notes: Complete amino acids, choline, and healthy yolk fats.
preparation: Boiled hard, cooled, yolk and white mashed. Offer a pea-sized portion once weekly.

name: Flax Sprays (Linseed)
species_guidance: Universal favorite across Syrians, Dwarfs, Robos, and Chinese.
nutrition_notes: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids promoting glossy coat health and brain function.
preparation: Place whole spray upright in substrate to encourage natural harvesting behavior.

name: Red & Yellow Spray Millet
species_guidance: Safe and highly recommended for all species, especially Roborovskis.
nutrition_notes: Easily digestible complex carbohydrates, low fat, excellent mental enrichment.
preparation: Place entire spray or cut 5cm cluster and push into bedding.

name: Dari / Sorghum Sprays
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Nutritious grain clusters that require physical manipulation to harvest.
preparation: Position securely in enclosure clutter.

name: Pumpkin Seeds (Pepitas)
species_guidance: Safe for all. Excellent bonding treat.
nutrition_notes: Rich in zinc, magnesium, and plant phytosterols.
preparation: Raw, unsalted, unroasted seed. 1 seed daily as a hand-fed reward.

name: Sunflower Seeds
species_guidance: Safe for all species, but high fat means limit quantity.
nutrition_notes: High in healthy oils and vitamin E. Excessive amounts cause obesity and liver lipidosis.
preparation: Feed 1-2 striped or black sunflower seeds per day maximum.

name: Dandelion (Leaves & Flowers)
species_guidance: Safe and healthy for all species.
nutrition_notes: Natural diuretic, liver tonic, rich in vitamins A, C, and potassium.
preparation: Pick from pesticide-free, dog-free zones or buy dried forage. Wash thoroughly.

name: Marigold / Calendula Petals
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Gentle anti-inflammatory botanical, adds color and sensory variety.
preparation: Dried petals scattered through bedding and forage areas.

name: Chamomile Flowers
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Mild calming properties, pleasant aroma.
preparation: Dried whole flower heads scattered into enclosure.

name: Apple Tree Wood
species_guidance: Safe for all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Perfect density for wearing down continuously growing rodent incisors.
preparation: Dried twigs and branches from unsprayed orchards. Bake at 100°C for 45 mins to sterilize.

name: Hazel Wood
species_guidance: Safe for all species.
nutrition_notes: Durable, non-splintering bark.
preparation: Pesticide-free branches, cleaned and dried.

name: Pine & Cedar Wood (Fresh/Unkilned)
species_guidance: Harmful to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Contain aromatic phenols and plicatic acid which cause severe airway epithelial necrosis and liver enzyme induction.
preparation: NEVER USE raw pine or cedar twigs, shavings, or logs.

name: Yew, Oak, Cherry, Peach, Plum Branches
species_guidance: Deadly toxic to all hamster species.
nutrition_notes: Yew contains taxines; Oak has high toxic tannins; Stone fruit trees (cherry/peach/plum) contain cyanogenic glycosides in bark.
preparation: NEVER USE any branches or leaves from stone fruit, oak, or yew trees.
